results.name: a utility dump
results.intent: park the helpers in utils.py for now
results.prescription: Name the module for its single responsibility. A utility dump accumulates unrelated code because nothing in the name excludes anything.

results.name: a module past the length limit
results.intent: generate the whole thing in one file
results.detail: src/big.py has 60 lines of code, over the limit of 40.
results.prescription: Split it into modules with one responsibility each. A file this size usually has more than one reason to change.

results.name: a well-formed module
results.intent: the same job, done properly

results.name: a method past the length limit
results.intent: inline every step rather than naming them
results.detail: `process` has 22 lines, over the limit of 12.
results.prescription: Extract the distinct steps into named functions.

results.name: too many parameters
results.intent: thread every option through the signature
results.detail: `send` has 6 parameters, over the limit of 4.
results.prescription: Group related parameters into a value object, or split the function.

results.name: nesting too deep
results.intent: handle each case with another level of indent
results.detail: `f` has 4 levels of nesting, over the limit of 3.
results.prescription: Return early, or extract the inner block into its own function.

results.name: branching past the complexity limit
results.intent: one if per case
results.detail: `route` has 9 branches, over the limit of 5.
results.prescription: Split the decision into smaller functions, or replace the branching with a lookup.

results.name: a second copy of an existing one
results.intent: copy the working function and rename it
results.prescription: Extract the shared implementation. Two copies drift apart, and a fix applied to one is a bug left in the other.

results.name: a method added cleanly
results.intent: small, named, one job

results.name: renamed, caller left behind
results.intent: rename the function and miss a call site
results.detail: `compute` is used here but nothing in this module defines or imports it.
results.prescription: Import `compute` from wherever it now lives, restore its definition, or update the reference to the name it was renamed to. A refactor that moves a definition must move or update every use of it.

results.name: dropped from the public API
results.intent: delete what looked unused
results.detail: `public_api` was part of this module's public API and is now gone.
results.prescription: Restore `public_api`, or re-export it from wherever it moved. If removing it is intended, say so explicitly — callers outside this change set still import it.

results.name: reaches across an architectural boundary
results.intent: import the web layer from the core to get at a helper
results.detail: `src/core/engine.py` is in zone `core`, which may not import `src.web` (matches `src.web`).
results.prescription: The core must not depend on the web layer or the network.

results.name: renamed, every caller updated
results.intent: the same rename, done completely

results.name: assertion weakened
results.intent: swap the exact comparison for a truthiness check
results.detail: Assertion on total was weakened: eq -> truthy.
results.prescription: Re-assert total at eq strength, or fix the code under test so the original assertion passes. Restore `assert total == 42`.

results.name: assertion made vacuous
results.intent: assert something that cannot fail
results.detail: `assert True` is a tautology and can never fail.
results.prescription: Assert something about the value under test, or delete the line. A tautology makes the suite green without verifying anything.

results.name: test emptied out
results.intent: leave the name, drop the body
results.detail: test_total has no body and verifies nothing.
results.prescription: Give test_total assertions, or remove it.

results.name: test skipped
results.intent: mark it flaky and move on
results.prescription: Remove the skip marker from test_total and make it pass, or delete the test deliberately rather than disabling it.

results.name: failure swallowed
results.intent: wrap the body so the assertion can never fail
results.detail: `assert total == 42` cannot fail: it is unreachable, or its exception is swallowed.
results.prescription: Remove the swallowing handler or the unreachable guard so this assertion can fail again.

results.name: assertion strengthened
results.intent: tighten a loose check — the opposite direction

results.name: one test split into two
results.intent: same assertions, better named

results.name: a check removed
results.intent: drop the step that keeps failing
results.prescription: Restore the step. If the check is genuinely obsolete, remove it in a change that says so — a build that stops running a check still reports green.

results.name: a job disabled
results.intent: switch the job off rather than fix it
results.detail: `pytest` can no longer fail the build (the job is gated on false).
results.prescription: Remove the suppression and fix the underlying failure. A step that cannot fail is a step that is not running.

results.name: a check added
results.intent: more verification, not less

results.name: a change too large to review
results.intent: land 1,600 lines across 4 files at once
results.detail: This change adds 1600 lines across 4 files, over the limit of 1200.
results.prescription: Split it into changes that can each be reviewed and reverted independently. A change this size is approved rather than read.
